title: Product Manager
description: Master end-to-end product management: customer discovery, metrics, feature prioritization, PRDs, agile execution, unit economics, PLG, stakeholder influence, and product strategy.

phases.title: Product Foundations
phases.focus: The PM Role, Continuous Discovery, Market Analysis & Customer Interviews

phases.title: Execution & Delivery
phases.focus: Metrics, Prioritization Frameworks, PRDs, Sprint Execution & Unit Economics

phases.title: Growth & Enterprise Scalability
phases.focus: Product-Led Growth, Stakeholder Influence, GTM Strategy & AI Product Management

phases.title: Strategy & Executive Leadership
phases.focus: Product Vision, Moats, Outcome Roadmaps, and Executive Communication

nodes.title: The Product Manager Role & Core Frameworks
nodes.subtitle: PM vs PO vs EM vs PMM, product lifecycle, Venn diagram (business, tech, UX), MVP definition
learning_objectives: Differentiate product management responsibilities from project management and engineering
Define minimum viable products (MVP) focused on maximum validated learning
feynman_prompts: Explain the primary role of a Product Manager in one sentence.
key_misconceptions: Assuming the PM is the 'CEO of the product' who issues orders to the team

nodes.title: Product Discovery & Problem Framing
nodes.subtitle: Customer problem vs solution trap, continuous discovery habits, Opportunity Solution Trees
learning_objectives: Construct Opportunity Solution Trees to link business outcomes to customer opportunities
Avoid the feature factory trap by validating problem severity before coding
feynman_prompts: What is the danger of jumping directly into feature specification without problem validation?
key_misconceptions: Accepting executive feature requests blindly without validating the underlying user need

nodes.title: Market Sizing & Competitive Intelligence
nodes.subtitle: TAM/SAM/SOM sizing, Porter's Five Forces, competitive positioning matrix, differentiation
learning_objectives: Calculate realistic TAM, SAM, and SOM figures for a new market opportunity
Map direct and indirect competitors on a 2x2 differentiation matrix
feynman_prompts: Explain the difference between TAM (Total Addressable Market) and SOM (Serviceable Obtainable Market).
key_misconceptions: Assuming a market has no competitors because no existing tool does the exact same thing

nodes.title: Customer Interviews & Insights for PMs
nodes.subtitle: The Mom Test framework, Jobs-To-Be-Done (JTBD), uncovering unarticulated needs
learning_objectives: Formulate Mom-Test-compliant questions that reveal past customer behavior
Structure customer needs into Jobs-To-Be-Done outcome statements
feynman_prompts: Why should you never ask customers 'Would you pay for a feature that does X?'
key_misconceptions: Taking customer feature suggestions literally instead of digging for their underlying pain point

nodes.title: Product Metrics & The North Star Framework
nodes.subtitle: North Star Metric (NSM), input metrics, Pirate Metrics (AARRR), leading vs lagging indicators
learning_objectives: Define an effective North Star Metric and 3-4 actionable leading input metrics
Deconstruct user journey telemetry using the AARRR (Pirate) funnel
feynman_prompts: Why is revenue usually a lagging indicator rather than an effective North Star Metric?
key_misconceptions: Tracking dozens of vanity metrics (pageviews, total signups) instead of actionable retention

nodes.title: Feature Prioritization Frameworks
nodes.subtitle: RICE (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort), MoSCoW, Kano Model, Cost of Delay
learning_objectives: Score competing product initiatives objectively using the RICE scoring model
Categorize product capabilities into baseline, performance, and delighter features (Kano)
feynman_prompts: How do you determine 'Confidence' scoring in RICE to prevent subjective bias?
key_misconceptions: Using prioritization frameworks to justify a gut-feeling decision made beforehand

nodes.title: PRDs, User Stories & Acceptance Criteria
nodes.subtitle: Product Requirement Documents, epics, user stories, INVEST criteria, Gherkin acceptance criteria
learning_objectives: Author clear, concise PRDs detailing problem, goals, out-of-scope items, and metrics
Write engineering-ready user stories with verifiable Gherkin acceptance criteria
feynman_prompts: What makes an acceptance criterion unambiguous for both engineering and QA?
key_misconceptions: Over-specifying technical implementation details in a PRD instead of user requirements and edge cases

nodes.title: Agile, Scrum & Sprint Execution for PMs
nodes.subtitle: Backlog grooming, sprint planning, daily standups, sprint reviews, managing tech debt
learning_objectives: Manage and groom a healthy product backlog prioritized by user and business value
Partner with engineering leads to allocate sprint capacity between features and technical debt
feynman_prompts: How should a PM handle scope creep discovered halfway through an active 2-week sprint?
key_misconceptions: Treating Agile as micro-managing engineers' daily hours rather than iterative value delivery

nodes.title: Product Analytics & A/B Testing
nodes.subtitle: Mixpanel/Amplitude cohort analysis, retention curves, hypothesis-driven experimentation
learning_objectives: Analyze user cohort retention curves to evaluate product-market fit
Design and interpret A/B test experiments with statistical significance thresholds
feynman_prompts: What does a flattening cohort retention curve indicate about product-market fit?
key_misconceptions: Declaring an A/B test a success based on click rates while ignoring cannibalization on downstream conversion

nodes.title: Unit Economics & Pricing Strategy
nodes.subtitle: CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC ratio, payback period, churn (gross vs net), freemium vs free trial
learning_objectives: Calculate Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)
Evaluate SaaS pricing tiers (usage-based, seat-based, tiered feature gating)
feynman_prompts: Explain why an LTV:CAC ratio below 3:1 is dangerous for SaaS sustainability.
key_misconceptions: Assuming that lowering prices is always the best strategy to increase conversion and retention

nodes.title: Product-Led Growth (PLG) & Virality
nodes.subtitle: Self-serve onboarding, time-to-value (TTV), virality coefficients (K-factor), expansion loops
learning_objectives: Design self-serve onboarding funnels that minimize time-to-value (TTV)
Engineer virality loops and organic invite mechanisms into product workflows
feynman_prompts: What is 'time-to-value' and why is it the defining metric of product-led onboarding?
key_misconceptions: Forcing users through multi-screen registration wizards before showing any product value

nodes.title: Stakeholder Management & Influencing Without Authority
nodes.subtitle: Stakeholder mapping, executive alignment, navigating sales vs eng friction, saying 'No'
learning_objectives: Navigate conflicting priorities across sales, marketing, engineering, and executives
Deliver principled, evidence-based 'No' responses while preserving relationships
feynman_prompts: How do you say 'No' to an urgent feature request from the enterprise sales team?
key_misconceptions: Saying 'Yes' to every stakeholder to avoid conflict, resulting in a fractured, unfocused product

nodes.title: Go-To-Market (GTM) Strategy & Product Marketing
nodes.subtitle: Positioning, messaging, launch tiers, cross-functional launch checklists, sales enablement
learning_objectives: Create compelling product positioning statements and value propositions
Coordinate cross-functional GTM launch execution across sales, support, and marketing
feynman_prompts: What is the difference between product features and customer-centric value messaging?
key_misconceptions: Treating product launch as the end of the project rather than the beginning of adoption

nodes.title: Technical Fluency for Product Managers
nodes.subtitle: APIs, microservices, databases, caching, webhooks, technical debt trade-offs
learning_objectives: Read API documentation and evaluate third-party integration technical feasibility
Have informed technical trade-off discussions regarding scalability vs delivery speed
feynman_prompts: Why is understanding API rate limits and async processing important for a non-coding PM?
key_misconceptions: Pretending to understand technical architecture instead of asking engineers clarifying questions

nodes.title: Enterprise B2B Product Management
nodes.subtitle: Multi-tenant architecture, RBAC, SSO, compliance (SOC2/GDPR), procurement cycles
learning_objectives: Design enterprise administration features (Single Sign-On, Role-Based Access Control)
Navigate enterprise security questionnaires, compliance, and procurement timelines
feynman_prompts: How do buyer personas differ from user personas in enterprise B2B sales cycles?
key_misconceptions: Assuming the person purchasing enterprise software is the person who will use it daily

nodes.title: AI Product Management & LLM Integration
nodes.subtitle: Evaluating LLM capabilities, prompt evaluation, non-deterministic UX, evals & guardrails
learning_objectives: Define evaluation metrics (precision, recall, ground truth accuracy) for AI features
Manage non-deterministic product edge cases and user trust boundaries
feynman_prompts: Why is deterministic software testing inadequate for evaluating LLM feature accuracy?
key_misconceptions: Treating AI as a plug-and-play feature without planning for latency, cost, and hallucination handling

nodes.title: Product Strategy & Vision Formulation
nodes.subtitle: Dhar/Gibson Biddle strategy models, Moats, DHM (Delight, Hard to copy, Margin-enhancing)
learning_objectives: Draft a compelling 3-5 year product vision anchored in clear strategic pillars
Build defensible competitive moats (network effects, switching costs, brand)
feynman_prompts: What is the difference between an operational roadmap and a strategic product vision?
key_misconceptions: Treating a chronological feature list as a product strategy

nodes.title: Executive Communication & Dynamic Roadmapping
nodes.subtitle: Outcome-based roadmaps (Now-Next-Later), QBRs, board presentations, crisis leadership
learning_objectives: Structure theme- and outcome-based roadmaps instead of rigid feature timelines
Present quarterly business reviews (QBR) and strategic pivots to executive leadership
feynman_prompts: Why are 'Now-Next-Later' roadmaps superior to calendar-based Gantt charts in agile product teams?
key_misconceptions: Committing to exact calendar delivery dates 12 months in advance in high-uncertainty environments
